Overflow & Coverage — screen mockup

The thin layer on top of HCHB Web Scheduling's exception queues. Left: what a flex clinician sees. Right: what the coordinator runs. Illustrative data only — no PHI.

Static mockup for stakeholder reaction. Every open visit shown is sourced from HCHB's Status Alerts or Smart Scheduling Exceptions queue; every card leads with pay; eligibility (scope, auth-ready, headroom) is enforced before a visit ever appears. Zones/ZIPs only — never patient address or name.

⚖︎ Fairness ledger: work spread across 9 clinicians this week · most-loaded flex clinician holds 3 extra visits · no concentration flag.   The unfilled RN Zone-A visit has recurred 3 wks → flagged as a structural coverage gap, not a one-off.

Row 5 shows the honest failure mode: when the board can’t fill it, the desk says so and escalates — a recurring gap is a staffing signal, not a coverage miss to paper over with agency.

What this mockup is asserting (for reaction, not committed design):
  • Demand is HCHB's, not ours — every row traces to the Status Alerts or Smart Scheduling Exceptions queue via visitId.
  • Pay leads — the earnings story is the reason a clinician opens the app (discovery §4).
  • Eligibility is pre-filtered — scope/SOC, auth-ready, and the FT headroom gate are enforced before a card shows; the clinician never sees a visit they can't lawfully take.
  • A "no" is free — penalty-free pass with a reason; the opt-in framing that avoids the Alabama failure.
  • Fairness + honesty are visible — the desk shows spread and flags a structural gap instead of hiding it behind agency spend.
